prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: roof tiles blown off in a storm. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"fact","content":"When the report says a few roof tiles were blown off in a storm but there is no sign of internal water ingress, I can usually triage it as external damage challenge."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I see missing tiles at the ridge, verge or eaves, I prefer to ask for close-up images from ground level and from inside the loft if safe, because open."},{"type":"preference","content":"When there is damage to gutters, fascia or soffits alongside the tiles, I prefer to treat the case as a roof-edge package rather than isolated tile loss, since
